reason: E1 shows ML potentials achieve near-DFT accuracy for a refractory high-entropy alloy, supporting the first premise. E2 demonstrates that vibrational entropy (including anharmonicity) can be extracted from AIMD displacement covariances for elemental Al and Na, supporting the second premise. However, no cited evidence supports the claims about active learning selectively capturing anharmonic configurations, the efficiency of umbrella integration for free energies, or the specific ~10x speed-up, leaving three key premises unsupported.
premises: ML potentials can be trained to near-DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys
Vibrational entropy can be captured from atomic displacement covariances in AIMD
Active learning can selectively sample key anharmonic configurations
Enhanced sampling (umbrella integration) can reconstruct free-energy profiles efficiently
The approach will reduce computational cost by ~10x vs full AIMD/TOR-TILD
